summary: Monthly update pass (docs/UPDATES.md) for newer editions of recurring publications listed as due on 2026-10-11: 33 documents stored and extracted (2723 numbers, 23 rules, 15 events). New Zealand AIP page, first MBIE AIP quarterly report and residence decisions (Sep 2026); Panama SNM permits Jan-Sep 2026; IMF St Kitts 2026, ECCU 2025 and 2026, Malta 2025, Comoros 2025; Dominica, Saint Lucia and Grenada budget documents; USCIS I-526 FY2026 Q3, DHS Yearbook FY2024, Macao IPIM quarterly tables 2025-2026; EC Montenegro 2025, Mauritius Finance Act 2026, Latvia PMLP 2025; India MHA, Italy MIMIT start-up reports, INCSR 2025, FATF June 2026 list. Where a new edition revises a figure already held, the new row is its own row and its notes name the earlier source.

sources.title: Active Investor Plus Visa statistics page (version last updated 2026-09-25)
sources.publisher: Immigration New Zealand (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
sources.covers: INZ Active Investor Plus statistics page, version with "Last update: 25 September 2026": pre-2025 settings summary; Table 1 pipeline and committed capital and Tables 3-4 applications by status and nationality, 1 April 2025 to 24 September 2026; Table 2 capital committed by investment type to 30 June 2026 (unchanged from the previous version); link to the first quarterly report.
sources.notes: Page updated in place; saved directly from the live page on 2026-10-11 (published_date is the "Last update" date printed on the page). From this version the headline pipeline-plus-committed total excludes withdrawn and declined applications. The page swaps the labels of two Table 2 rows (infrastructure and fund of funds) compared with the MBIE quarterly report.

sources.title: Quarterly report on the Active Investor Plus visa - Q4 FY25/26 (briefing REQ-0035597, proactive release)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (Immigration New Zealand)
sources.covers: MBIE briefing to the Ministers of Immigration and of Trade and Investment dated 31 July 2026 on AIP in April-June 2026 and cumulatively since 1 April 2025: applications by month, category, status and top nationalities; regional shares; processing times; capital committed by type in Q4 and cumulatively; pipeline; Invest NZ May 2026 recertification of managed funds (funds approved, capital committed, deployed and undeployed by fund type; commitment trend; sectors); OIO consents for home purchases by region.
sources.notes: Proactive release (coversheet: date to be published 18 September 2026), linked from the INZ AIP statistics page; some names withheld for privacy. Amounts printed with a bare "$" are New Zealand dollars (NZ government document). The page says the report is one of a quarterly series; earlier quarters are not linked from the page.

sources.title: Statistics — residence decisions by financial year (edition prepared 8 October 2026)
sources.publisher: Immigration New Zealand
sources.covers: Resident visa applications decided (approved/declined) and people included, by application criteria and financial year (Jul-Jun) 2016/17 to 2026/27 (to 30 Sep 2026), by month for July-September 2026, and by nationality and substream. Rows for Investor 1, Investor 2, Active Investor Plus and Active Investor Plus (Growth or Balanced); Investor Category column in the nationality tables.
sources.notes: Report prepared 8 Oct 2026 ('10/8/2026', US date format). Same 98-page layout as the September edition (nzl-inz-residence-decisions-2026), replaced in place at the same address. INZ 'declined' includes applications withdrawn at the client's request or replaced. 2026/27 covers July-September 2026 only. One August 2026 cell for AIP (Growth or Balanced) changed by one between editions.

sources.title: Permisos de residencia: año 2026 (cifras preliminares al 30 de septiembre del 2026)
sources.publisher: Servicio Nacional de Migración (SNM), Panamá
sources.covers: January-September 2026 residence permits decided, approved and denied by month; approved by type, sex, category (p. 2) and country, and by age (p. 3). Approvals only by category.
sources.notes: Preliminary figures to 30 Sep 2026 'sujetas a revisión y actualización'. PDF created 9 Oct 2026 (published_date taken from the file's creation date). The server reset the first connections; the file downloaded on a later attempt. New in this edition: a separate 'SOLVENCIA PROPIA-INVERSION MIXTA' row (earlier 2026 editions folded it into 'Otras categorías'). Some September cells of out-of-scope categories repeat earlier months' values (PPSH 2,021 as in August; Dependientes 818 as in July), possibly a compilation slip.

sources.title: St. Kitts and Nevis: 2026 Article IV Consultation-Press Release and Staff Report (IMF Country Report No. 26/93)
sources.publisher: International Monetary Fund
sources.covers: CBI revenue % GDP 2019-2031 (text table, Tables 1-2), CBI due diligence fees and CBI dividend % GDP 2021-2031, balances excluding CBI, authorities' 2026 CBI budget (St Kitts and Nevis split), CBI capital-account inflows 2020-2025, ECCIRA approval (Oct 2025) and Sovereign Wealth and Resilience Fund bill (Feb 2026).
sources.notes: Direct curl from imf.org (source PDF); eLibrary landing page https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2026/093/002.2026.issue-093-en.xml. Staff report dated 2 April 2026; 79 pages. Column 2025 marked Est., 2026-2031 Proj.

sources.title: Eastern Caribbean Currency Union: 2026 Discussion on Common Policies of Member Countries-Press Release and Staff Report (IMF Country Report No. 26/85)
sources.publisher: International Monetary Fund
sources.covers: ECCU central government overall balance excluding CBI, 2021-2027 (Table 1); CBI revenue share of total non-grant revenue in 2025 by country (Key Vulnerabilities table); ECCIRA and CBI data-transparency recommendations.
sources.notes: Direct curl from imf.org (source PDF). 88 pages. Column 2025 marked Est., 2026-2027 Proj. Country-level CBI revenue charts carry no printed values.

sources.title: Eastern Caribbean Currency Union: 2025 Staff Report for the 2025 Discussion on Common Policies of Member Countries-Press Release; and Staff Report (IMF Country Report No. 25/104)
sources.publisher: International Monetary Fund
sources.covers: ECCU overall balance excluding CBI 2020-2026 (Table 1); underlying deficit net of CBI 2023-2024; change in total CBI revenue 2024; estimated range of total CBI inflows 2019-2023 (chart with printed values); common minimum pricing June 2024 and regional regulator work.
sources.notes: Wayback copy of the print PDF (imf.org answered HTTP 429 to curl). 85 pages. Column 2024 marked Est., 2025-2026 Proj.; projections based on information as of 31 March 2025.

sources.title: Eastern Caribbean Currency Union: Selected Issues (IMF Country Report No. 25/105)
sources.publisher: International Monetary Fund
sources.covers: Chapter "ECCU CBI Programs: Regional Significance and Risks" (PDF pp. 13-19): overview of the five programmes (investment options, holding periods, data published), CBI revenue in percent of non-grant revenue 2019 and 2023 by country, estimated range of total CBI inflows 2019-2023, direct CBI project investment vs FDI and total inflows vs tourism exports 2023, 2023 Roundtable principles and March 2024 Memorandum of Agreement (US$200,000 minimum).
sources.notes: Wayback copy of the print PDF. Companion to IMF CR 25/104. Several charts (CBI revenue % GDP and EC$ millions 2014-2025, minimum qualifying investment, applications received) print no values.

sources.title: Malta: 2025 Article IV Consultation-Press Release and Staff Report (IMF Country Report No. 26/29)
sources.publisher: International Monetary Fund
sources.covers: No content on investor citizenship or residence: no IIP/MEIN proceeds lines in the fiscal tables; immigration discussed only as labour migration (Annex VII).
sources.notes: Direct curl from imf.org (source PDF). 67 pages. Board discussion 4 February 2026. The companion Selected Issues (CR 26/30) was also checked and has no programme content (not stored).

sources.title: Union of the Comoros: 2025 Article IV Consultation, Fifth Review under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement, and Request for Waivers of Nonobservance of Performance Criteria-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for the Union of the Comoros (IMF Country Report No. 26/47)
sources.publisher: International Monetary Fund

sources.notes: Wayback copy (imf.org answered HTTP 429 to curl). 139 pages.

sources.title: Estimates 2026/2027 (draft)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Commonwealth of Dominica
sources.covers: Draft estimates volume for FY2026/27 (426 pages): CBI revenue by item (actual 2024/25, estimate and projected 2025/26, budget 2026/27, forward 2027/28-2028/29), Citizenship by Investment Unit expenditure programme, CBI share of revenue and of recurrent expenditure, CBI posts.
sources.notes: Listed on finance.gov.dm/en/publications/estimates/2026-2027-draft-estimates; PDF created 26 July 2026. Unlike the 2025/26 volume, the revenue detail pages have a text layer; the revenue summary (p. 31), pie chart (p. 30) and standard-object analysis (p. 9) are images, read from the page image or by OCR. Downloaded over http.

sources.title: 2025-2026 Estimates of Revenue & Expenditure
sources.publisher: Department of Finance, Government of Saint Lucia
sources.covers: Estimates volume FY2025/26 (939 pages): contribution from the National Economic (Development) Fund to revenue 2023/24-2027/28; National Economic Fund row among grants in the summary (zeros); NEF project financing (zero); 15 CIP government bonds in the external debt schedule (balance at 31 Dec 2024, principal repayment 2025/26).

sources.title: 2026-2027 Estimates of Revenue & Expenditure

sources.notes: Download file name Estimates_of_Expenditure_26_27-(1).pdf; posted 28 July 2026 per the resources list (PDF created 25 June 2026). New chart of accounts (revenue codes 11251005 etc.).

sources.title: Montenegro 2025 Report, Commission Staff Working Document, SWD(2025) 754 final/2
sources.publisher: European Commission
sources.covers: EC yearly enlargement report on Montenegro (110 pp.). Investor citizenship scheme: 2024 decisions (1,282; 385 applicants and 899 family members), 2024 grants by nationality (Russia 709, Belarus 42, Saudi Arabia 29), 21 applications still being processed; recommendation to repeal the legal basis and revoke citizenship of sanctioned persons.
sources.notes: Corrected version ('final/2') of SWD(2025) 754, dated 4.11.2025. The 385 + 899 split adds to 1,284, not the 1,282 printed in the same sentence.

sources.title: The Finance Act 2026 (Act No. 14 of 2026)
sources.publisher: Republic of Mauritius (copy hosted by the Mauritius Revenue Authority)
sources.covers: Finance Act implementing the Budget 2026-2027 (28 sections, 10 schedules; Acts 2026 pp. 443-...). In scope: repeal of the 2025 special registration duty and 10% land transfer tax for non-citizen transfers of EDB-scheme property; new 10% additional duty on transfers to non-citizens of residential property on State land or Pas Geometriques; 'golden visa' added to the Income Tax Act premium-visa provisions.
sources.notes: Published date is the date of assent (12 August 2026); the Government Gazette date is not printed in this copy. Passed by the National Assembly on 31 July 2026. Unlike 2025, it does not amend the EDB Act, the Immigration Act 2022 or the Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act.

sources.title: Pilsonības un migrācijas lietu pārvaldes publiskais pārskats 2025 (PMLP public annual report 2025)
sources.publisher: Pilsonības un migrācijas lietu pārvalde (Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs, PMLP)
sources.covers: PMLP 2025 annual report (62 pp.): budget, migration (residence permits issued 69,888; first-time 15,928; visas; returns), asylum, identity documents, population register, citizenship, staff. No figures or text on residence permits for investors.
sources.notes: Unlike the 2014-2015 reports, the 2025 report says nothing about the investor residence permits.

sources.title: Annual Report 2024-25
sources.publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India

sources.notes: The file name (AREnglish_24032026) suggested a 2025-26 report, but the cover says "Annual Report 2024-25" and the MHA annual-reports page lists it as "Annual Report Ministry of Home Affairs 2024-2025". It does not mention permanent residency status for foreign investors.

sources.title: 2025 International Narcotics Control Strategy Report, Volume II: Money Laundering
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs
sources.covers: INCSR 2025 Vol. II (305 pp.): comparative table and country reports on money laundering, mostly about 2024. Short passages on citizenship-by-investment programmes in Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, St Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Cyprus, El Salvador, Peru and Nicaragua.
sources.notes: Figures about programmes are the State Department relaying other bodies (status reported). "$" in a US federal document is read as US dollars. The 2025 edition has no offshore-centre table with a "sells economic citizenship" column (unlike the 2002-2003 editions).

sources.title: Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring - 19 June 2026
sources.publisher: Financial Action Task Force
sources.covers: FATF grey list after the June 2026 plenary: 22 jurisdictions under increased monitoring, two newly identified (Bosnia and Herzegovina, Iraq), two removed (Algeria, Namibia).
sources.notes: fatf-gafi.org answers HTTP 403 to scripts; the stored copy is the Wayback Machine capture of 1 Oct 2026 (HTML). Newest list as of 11 Oct 2026; the October 2026 plenary had not yet met. Lists from June 2024 to February 2026 are not stored.

observations.location: PDF p. 52 (printed p. 51), Chapter 23, Citizenship rights
observations.quote: In 2024, the Ministry of Internal Affairs issued 1 282 decisions on granting Montenegrin citizenship in line with the provisions of the investor citizenship scheme (385 for applicants and 899 for family members).
observations.notes: Decisions granting citizenship in 2024 on applications lodged before the scheme expired on 31 Dec 2022; the EC counts per person (applicants and family members). Same figure as intl-ec-com-2025-792 and intl-ec-swd-2025-429; repeated on PDF p. 61. The split printed in the same sentence (385 applicants + 899 family members) adds to 1,284, two more than the 1,282 total.

observations.location: PDF p. 61, Chapter 24, Legal and irregular migration / visa policy
observations.quote: In 2024, 1282 individuals were granted Montenegrin citizenship through pending applications of the investor citizenship scheme which ended on 31 December 2022. events.title: National Assembly approves agreement establishing the regional CBI regulator (ECCIRA)
events.description: St Kitts and Nevis' National Assembly approved the agreement among Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, St Kitts and Nevis and St Lucia to establish the Eastern Caribbean Citizenship by Investment Regulatory Authority, which oversees and regulates all persons operating the programme, with offences, penalties and enforcement powers.
events.quote: The National Assembly of St. Kitts and Nevis approved the agreement on October 17, 2025.

events.title: Sovereign Wealth and Resilience Fund bill, to receive CIU profits and SISC revenue, has first reading
events.description: The bill would channel into a new Sovereign Wealth and Resilience Fund up to 25 percent of the profits of the Citizenship by Investment Unit and the revenue the CIU collects as Sustainable Island State Contributions, plus Geothermal Energy Authority profits. Not yet enacted when the IMF report was written.
events.location: PDF p. 20 (printed p. 16), para 16 and footnote 21
events.quote: The proposed legislation would channel into the new fund up to 25 percent of the profits of the CIU, the profits collected by the Geothermal Energy Authority, and the revenue collected by the CIU identified as Sustainable Island State Contributions. The first reading by the National Assembly took place on February 12, 2026.

events.title: Commission: repeal the legal basis for an investor citizenship scheme
events.description: EC Montenegro 2025 Report: to comply with EU law Montenegro should repeal the legal basis allowing the scheme to be (re)developed; it should run security checks on the remaining applications and revoke citizenship granted through the scheme to persons under international restrictive measures.
events.quote: To ensure compliance with EU law, Montenegro should repeal the legal basis allowing for the (re)development of an investor citizenship scheme.

events.title: 2025 duty basis and 10% resale tax for non-citizen scheme property repealed
events.description: The Finance Act 2026 repeals the Registration Duty Act s. 3(1G) and paragraph K of Part I of its First Schedule (the duty basis for deeds transferring EDB Property Scheme or NCPRA s. 3(3)(c)(v) residential property to non-citizens from 1 July 2026, added by the Finance Act 2025), and repeals s. 4(9) of the Land (Duties and Taxes) Act (the 10% land transfer tax on such transfers by a non-citizen). Neither repeal is given a separate date in s. 28, so both take effect with the Act; the date of assent is used.

events.title: 10% additional duty on State-land residential property sold to non-citizens
events.description: The Finance Act 2026 adds s. 4(11) to the Land (Duties and Taxes) Act: an additional duty of 10%, paid by the seller, on deeds transferring residential property on State land or Pas Geometriques to a non-citizen under s. 3(3)(c)(v) of the Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act. It does not apply where a notarised presale agreement was signed before 19 June 2026. Not given a separate date in s. 28; the date of assent is used.
events.quote: an additional duty shall be levied on any deed witnessing the transfer of a residential property located on State land or on Pas Géométriques to a non-citizen under section 3(3)(c)(v) of the Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act

events.title: 'Golden visa' added to the Income Tax Act's premium-visa provisions
events.description: The Finance Act 2026 defines a 'golden visa' as a visa issued under the Passports Act to a non-citizen on the recommendation of the Economic Development Board, and extends Income Tax Act ss. 73B and 74A(2)(a) (premium visa holders) to golden visa holders. The Act does not say what a golden visa requires; no programme is linked until a document sets out its conditions.
events.quote: “golden visa” means a visa issued by the passport officer under the Passports Act to a non-citizen on the recommendation of the Economic Development Board;

events.title: US INCSR 2025: Antigua and Barbuda CBI excludes six nationalities and has suspended Russia and Belarus
events.description: The State Department's 2025 money laundering report says the programme grants citizenship after criminal background checks, that nationals of Iran, Iraq, North Korea, Yemen, Somalia and Sudan are ineligible, and that Antigua and Barbuda states it suspended applications from Russia and Belarus as of February 2022.
events.location: PDF p. 56, Antigua and Barbuda, Overview
events.quote: Nationals of Iran, Iraq, North Korea, Yemen, Somalia, and Sudan are ineligible to apply. Antigua and Barbuda states it suspended CBI applications from Russia and Belarus as of February 2022.

events.title: US INCSR 2025: investigations into the terminated Cyprus programme ongoing
events.description: The State Department's 2025 report says Cyprus terminated its CBI programme in 2020 amid allegations of corruption and that related investigations are ongoing and have led to prosecutions and/or revocations of citizenship (no numbers).
events.quote: The ROC terminated its citizenship by investment (CBI) program in 2020 amid allegations of corruption. Investigations related to the CBI are ongoing and have led to prosecutions and/or revocations of citizenship.

events.title: US INCSR 2025: Nicaragua offers an expedited path to citizenship for investors
events.description: The State Department's 2025 report says Nicaragua grants asylum and citizenship to individuals perceived as political allies and offers an expedited path to citizenship for investors (no amounts).
events.quote: Nicaragua grants asylum and citizenship to individuals perceived as political allies and offers an expedited path to citizenship for investors.

events.title: Bulgaria placed under FATF increased monitoring (grey list)

events.quote: In October 2023, Bulgaria made a high-level political commitment to work with the FATF and MONEYVAL to strengthen the effectiveness of its AML/CFT regime.

new_indicators.name: Programme capital deployed by investment vehicles
new_indicators.definition: Money that programme investors committed to an investment vehicle (e.g. a managed fund) which the vehicle has called and invested in underlying businesses or assets, at a date, as reported by the authority. Excludes capital committed but uncalled or held as cash.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by updates-2026-10 for the Invest NZ recertification check in the MBIE AIP quarterly report Q4 FY2025/26 (Annex Two Table One).

new_indicators.name: Programme capital committed but not deployed
new_indicators.definition: Money committed by programme investors to an investment vehicle that has not yet been called or is held as cash by the vehicle, at a date, as reported by the authority.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by updates-2026-10 (MBIE AIP quarterly report Q4 FY2025/26, Annex Two Table One, column "Not deployed (uncalled or cash held)").

new_indicators.name: Share of committed programme capital deployed
new_indicators.definition: Percentage of programme capital committed to investment vehicles that has been deployed, at a date, as printed by the source. Never calculated by us.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by updates-2026-10 (MBIE AIP quarterly report Q4 FY2025/26).

new_indicators.name: Programme investment funds meeting a stated condition
new_indicators.definition: Number of approved programme investment funds that meet a condition the source states (measure=received_capital: funds that have received programme capital; measure=invested_in_sector: funds with programme-funded investment in the sector given by sector=), at a date. Not the number of funds approved (eligible_investment_funds).
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by updates-2026-10 (MBIE AIP quarterly report Q4 FY2025/26, Annex Two Tables One and Three).

new_indicators.name: Consents for property purchases granted to programme participants
new_indicators.definition: Consents or permissions granted by a regulator (e.g. the New Zealand Overseas Investment Office) allowing programme visa holders to buy or build residential property outside the programme route, at a date or in a period. Consents, not completed purchases.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by updates-2026-10 (MBIE AIP quarterly report Q4 FY2025/26, para 19 and Table Four). Not property_purchases_by_programme_participants, which counts completed purchases.

new_indicators.name: Change in CBI revenue to government, percentage points of GDP
new_indicators.definition: Change in CBI revenue to government as a share of GDP between two periods, in percentage points, as printed by the source (negative for a fall). Never calculated by us.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by updates-2026-10 (IMF CR 26/93 and 25/104 state changes only in percentage points).

new_indicators.name: CBI inflows as a share of tourism exports
new_indicators.definition: Total programme inflows (donations plus direct investment) in a period as a percentage of tourism (travel) exports, as estimated by the source.
